jobs.title: Investigator
jobs.description:
*Investigator - Calgary*

The Alberta Motor Vehicle Industry Council (AMVIC) is Alberta's automotive industry regulator. AMVIC is a public agency accountable to the Minister of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction and the Government of Alberta. AMVIC protects consumers and industry from unfair practices in the automotive business industry. Consumer protection and a fair marketplace are achieved through AMVIC-managed mandatory licensing for automotive businesses and salesperson registrations as required by the Consumer Protection Act.

AMVIC is responsible for the enforcement of the Consumer Protection Act, Automotive Business Regulation and related automotive regulations in the province of Alberta. Investigators are responsible for investigating consumer and industry complaints relating to the motor vehicle industry in Alberta, including automotive and recreational vehicle sales, repair and service. AMVIC is also responsible for investigating fraudulent activities in the motor vehicle industry.

This is a permanent full-time Investigator position based in Calgary, Alberta. The ideal candidate is an experienced investigator from any industry sector who can independently conduct and document investigations while working effectively with the general public, businesses, industry associations, and law enforcement agencies.

The position reports to the Manager of Investigations, South based in the Calgary office. The position will be home based, Monday to Friday, and requires some overnight travel to communities in Alberta.

*Responsibilities will include:*
- Conduct all investigations fairly and objectively and in accordance with the requirements of the Consumer Protection Act and Regulations, Criminal Code of Canada, Traffic Safety Act, Canada Evidence Act, Provincial Offences Procedure Act and the Protection of Privacy Protection Act (POPA) and Access to Information Act (ATIA).
- Conduct all investigations and enforcement activities in accordance with AMVIC policies in a timely fashion.
- Investigate consumer and industry complaints.
- Network with municipal business licensing offices, Bylaw Officers and police services on a regular basis.
- Identify unlicensed businesses and salespeople and take appropriate action.
- Submit reports on emerging issues and enforcement activity as required.
- Experience investigator - trainer role for newly hired investigators.

*Qualifications and technical skills:*
- Successful completion of post-secondary diploma or degree in law, business, finance or related field or a journeyman certification.
- Minimum five years' experience as an investigator in a law enforcement environment, inspector/Investigator in a regulatory compliance environment, OR combination of law enforcement, regulatory and experience in the automotive industry.
- Knowledge of Alberta's Consumer Protection Act; Automotive Business Regulation; Cost of Credit Disclosure Regulation; Internet Sales Contract Regulation; Alberta Traffic Safety Act; Criminal Code of Canada; Canada Evidence Act; Alberta Peace Officer Act; and the Protection of Privacy Protection Act and Access to Information Act
- Complete the Peace Officer training requirements and maintain Peace Officer status
- Conducting investigations and taking of formal statements
- Understanding of all court procedures, including exhibit handling
- Practical workings of the automotive industry
- Experience working with major case files.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- Computer skills with above average keyboarding skills
- Experience and ability to organize large investigative files
- Experience in working with Legislation, Acts and regulations
- Ability to work from home (home office)
- Candidate may be required to successfully complete a criminal record check

*AMVIC offers:*
- Competitive compensation.
- Excellent group health benefits.
- Group RRSP after one-year of employment.

Pay: From $80,331.00 per year

Benefits:
- Dental care
- Disability insurance
- Employee assistance program
- Extended health care
- Life insurance
- Mileage reimbursement
- RRSP match
- Wellness program

Licence/Certification:
- Valid Class 5 Drivers license (required)

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Calgary, AB T2W 4Y1

jobs.description:
Job Information

Job Requisition ID: 86341
Ministry: Transportation and Economic Corridors
Location: Calgary
Full or Part-Time: Full Time
Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week
Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent
Scope: Open Competition
Closing Date: August 28, 2026
Classification: Standards Safety Compliance 5
Salary: 3,477.50 to 4,334.98 bi-weekly ($90,726 - $113,142 /year)

Alberta Transportation and Economic Corridors (TEC) is a centre of excellence for transportation in North America.

Role Responsibilities

Reporting to the Lead Investigator, Vehicle Safety, you will provide technical assistance to licensed facilities, technicians, registered owners, carrier companies, law enforcement partners and the general public. This role will conduct complex investigations, facility and vehicle inspections using their knowledge of the safety standards and appropriate legislation to promote public safety.

The VSI coordinates leads and undertakes investigations, into alleged non-compliance with provincial Acts and Regulations.
Responsible for conducting facility and vehicle inspections using their knowledge of the vehicle safety standards and appropriate legislation to promote public safety.
The VSI will consider all aspects of the investigation results and make decisions based upon appropriate progressive discipline policy that range from Vehicle Safety Directives to Administrative Penalty.
The incumbent will lead or participate in joint investigations with internal and external stakeholders; Law enforcement agencies, Service Alberta
Document statements and evidence for investigative files, proper practice on statement procedures for court presentation and disciplinary hearings.
Exercise powers granted under an Investigators designation to ensure the safety of the motoring public.
Analyze documents including Records of Inspection, Inspection Certificates, decals, invoices, and Requests for Inspection.
Maintain existing, and develop new, enforcement agency relationships as well as inter-governmental relationships.
Complete administrative duties as assigned including court ready reports and updating vehicle status.

Qualifications

Required:
Journeyperson level certification and 5 years related experience at the Journeyperson level;
or Two Journeyperson level certifications and 3 years related experience at the Journeyperson level;
or Related degree and 3 years related experience.
Eligibility for appointment as an investigator.

Assets:
Preference will be given to incumbents who possess two Journeyperson certifications and/or enforcement and technical training.
Expert knowledge of the Traffic Safety Act and all supporting regulations
Extensive knowledge and experience with investigative procedures and requirements for conducting investigations.
Certification in the North American Standard Inspection Program.
Broad exposure to vehicle maintenance and transportation industries

Notes

Term of Employment: Permanent
Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week.
Location: Calgary
Travel is essential and mandatory for this position at a rate of 25% - 50%.
Cover Letter: Please provide a cover letter outlining your skills, knowledge and experience as they relate to the role.

jobs.title: Calgary Police Service - Digital Evidence Technician
jobs.description:
If you are committed to public service, enjoy collaborating with others, share our values and have a desire to learn and grow, join The City of Calgary. City employees deliver the services, run the programs and operate the facilities which make a difference in our community.

As a Digital Evidence Technician, you will support all areas of the Calgary Police Service (CPS) by extracting data from various electronic devices (computers, cellular phones and other various data storage devices) for digital evidence. Specific duties include:

Maintain the intake and extraction of electronic devices and ensure the preservation of data is maintained by providing detailed notes and creating formal reports.
Provide deskside support and guidance to police investigators who will be reviewing digital evidence related to the investigation to support investigated offences.
Assist in reviewing, organizing & retention of data such as photos, videos, text messages, social media information and any data related to the offence.
Provide technical support, troubleshoot technical issues and maintain records and historical tracking data.
Maintain up to date knowledge of industry standard software that is used daily to ensure the integrity of the evidence for future court purposes.
Perform administrative duties including restocking supplies, printing, photocopying.

Working Conditions: This position is regularly exposed to graphic, disturbing and sensitive materials.

Qualifications
A 1-year Certificate in Criminal Justice, Video Technology, Computer Science or related discipline and a minimum of 3 years related experience.
CompTIA A+ Certification (or equivalent) is required.
Previous experience in a law enforcement or justice-based environment will be considered an asset.
Success in this position requires commitment and dedication to continuous learning and professional development.

Pre-employment Requirements
An enhanced security clearance and pre-employment polygraph will be conducted.
Successful applicants must provide proof of qualifications.

Position and Pay Information

Business Unit: Calgary Police Services
Union: CUPE Local 38
Position Type: 1 Permanent
Compensation: Pay Grade 7 $36.60 - 48.97 per hour
Hours of work: Standard 35 hour work week.
Days of work: This position works a 5 day work week with 1 day off in a 3 week cycle.
Location: 5111 47 Street N.E.
Audience: Internal/External
Apply By: August 18, 2026
Job ID: 315101
